deeds-tripura.title: Burning of the three cities (Tripura)
deeds-tripura.brief: Three flying cities of the demons Tarakaksha, Kamalaksha and Vidyunmali made them unconquerable. The gods made Shiva a chariot: Meru the bow, Vishnu the arrow, Vasuki the string. When the cities aligned he destroyed them with one smile or arrow. A Tamil tradition has Ganesha breaking the chariot's axle before the battle (song 1).

refs.gist: Narada tells how Maya built the three cities of gold, silver and iron; Shiva's arrows burn them, Maya revives the dead in a nectar well, Vishnu intervenes
Karna parva: Shiva with the Pashupata missile and the divine chariot burns the Tripura; told as a model for Karna's chariot
Short allusions: Shiva as destroyer of Tripura
Allusion: Shiva's bow given by the gods for the Tripura fight; Shiva-Vishnu bow contest
Nandikeshvara narrates the Tripura demons and the construction of Rudra's chariot for their burning

deeds-kama.title: Kama burned by the forehead eye
deeds-kama.brief: The gods sent Kama, god of love, to break Shiva's meditation so that he would marry Parvati and father a commander for their army. Shiva opened his forehead eye and burned Kama to ash; Rati's grief won Kama a bodiless life (Ananga).

refs.gist: Kama attacked Shiva, was burned by his eye, became Ananga; origin of the Anga country

deeds-poison.title: Shiva drinks the Halahala poison
deeds-poison.brief: When the gods and demons churned the milk ocean, the Halahala poison rose and threatened the worlds. Shiva drank it at the gods' plea; Parvati held his throat and the poison stayed there, turning it blue (Neelakantha).

refs.gist: Devas approach Shiva; Bhavani consents; Shiva drinks the poison, his throat turns blue

refs.gist: Bhagiratha's year of penance; Shiva agrees to bear Ganga; she falls on his head and is held in his matted locks; released at Bindu lake

deeds-ravana.title: Ravana lifts Kailasa
deeds-ravana.brief: Ravana tried to lift Mount Kailasa. Shiva pressed it down with his toe and crushed Ravana's arms. After a long cry and hymns Ravana was released; the name Ravana is explained as 'the one who roared'.

refs.gist: Ravana on the Pushpaka is stopped by Nandi at Kailasa, scorns him, tries to uproot the mountain; Shiva presses it and he cries out, gaining the name Ravana

deeds-sarabha.title: Shiva as Sarabha
deeds-sarabha.brief: After Narasimha killed Hiranyakashipu his rage did not cool. Shiva took the form of the fierce Sarabha (part lion, part bird) and calmed him. The story is told in later Puranas and Shaiva tradition.

murugan-skanda-birth.title: Murugan born from Shiva's eye
murugan-skanda-birth.brief: Six sparks from Shiva's forehead eye were carried by Agni and Ganga to the Saravana pool and became six babies, nursed by the six Krittikas. Uma joined them into one six-faced child.
